jobs.occupation: Senior Data Engineer - Animal Health Clinical Development (m/w/d) (Data Engineer)
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Tasks & responsibilities

- Act as a trusted partner to business stakeholders, translating business needs into scalable, sustainable technology and data solutions.
- Design, implement, and support Clinical Development data platforms and cloud-based data services across the Animal Health ecosystem.
- Enable efficient data acquisition, integration, transformation, analytics, and reporting through modern AWS-based solutions.
- Drive data interoperability, system integration, and enterprise-wide information exchange across clinical, regulatory, and business platforms.
- Implement DataOps, automation, and operational excellence practices to improve quality, scalability, efficiency, and user experience.
- Lead data governance, platform strategy, and the evolution of future data management capabilities, including metadata, semantic technologies, and interoperability frameworks.
- Collaborate with business, scientific, and IT stakeholders to identify opportunities, modernize technology landscapes, and deliver value-driven solutions.
- Provide technical leadership, project oversight, mentoring, and stakeholder engagement while ensuring compliance with enterprise architecture, security, and data standards.

Requirements

- Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, Life Sciences Informatics or a related field or a Bachelor's degree with more relevant professional experience.
- Several years of professional experience in DataOps, Data Engineering, Data Integration, Clinical Systems, or Data Platform Engineering, preferably within pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences environments.
- Strong expertise in data modeling, data integration, and end-to-end data management processes.
- Hands-on experience with cloud-based data platforms and services, preferably AWS, including modern analytics solutions such as Snowflake or Databricks.
- Experience developing and supporting ETL/ELT pipelines, API integrations, and data interoperability solutions.
- Strong programming and scripting skills (Python preferred), along with experience in relational databases and data architecture concepts.
- Knowledge of containerization and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, or similar) and GxP-regulated environments, including data governance, quality, security, and compliance.
- Demonstrated project delivery, stakeholder management, communication, and teamwork skills, with a proactive, solution-oriented, and accountable mindset.
- Fluent English skills are required.

As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.
Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.
With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

jobs.occupation: PhD Student (f/m/d) Charge-to-Spin Interconversion and Magnetotransport in Altermagnetic Thin Films (Physiker/in)
jobs.description:
PhD Student (f/m/d) Charge-to-Spin Interconversion and Magnetotransport in Altermagnetic Thin Films

With cutting-edge research in the fields of ENERGY, HEALTH and MATTER, around 1,500 employees from more than 70 nations at Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) are committed to mastering the great challenges facing society today.

The Institute for Ion Beam Physics and Materials Research is dedicated to the study of materials and their nanostructures that can be considered for future applications in information technology and are based on electrical, magnetic or optical functionalities.

The Department of Magnetism is looking for a PhD Student (f/m/d) on Charge-to-Spin Interconversion and Magnetotransport in Altermagnetic Thin Films.

Your tasks

- Deposition and optimization of high-quality altermagnetic thin films and heterostructures
- Structural and magnetic characterization
- Investigation of magnetotransport phenomena and charge-to-spin interconversion
- Exploration of the fundamental spintronic properties of altermagnetic materials

Your profile

- Completed university studies (Master/Diploma) in the field of experimental physics or related field
- Background in eletric transport and magnetism
- Knowledge in thin film preparation and characterization techniques
- A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for working in an international research team
- Proficiency in German and/or English

Our offer

- A vibrant research community in an open, diverse and international work environment
- Scientific excellence and extensive professional networking opportunities
- A structured PhD program with a comprehensive range of continuing education and networking opportunities - more information about the PhD program at the HZDR can be found here (https://www.hzdr.de/db/Cms?pNid=1908)
- Salary and social benefits in accordance with the collective agreement for the public sector (TVöD-Bund) including 30 days of paid holiday leave, company pension scheme (VBL)
- Depending on the personal qualifications, the candidate may be classified in salary group 13 according to TVöD-Bund
- We support a good work-life balance with the possibility of part-time employment, mobile working and flexible working hours
- Numerous company health management offerings
- Employee discounts with well-known providers via the platform Corporate Benefits
- An employer subsidy for the "Deutschland-Ticket Jobticket"

We look forward to receiving your application documents (including cover letter, CV, diplomas/transcripts, etc.), which you can submit via our online-application-system.

The TRR404 “Next Generation Electronics With Active Devices in Three Dimensions [Active-3D]” is a Collaborative Research Center/Transregio between TUD Dresden University of Technology and Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule Aachen (RWTH Aachen) funded by Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft. The TRR aims at exploring a completely new approach for microelectronics technology and therefore teams up materialists, electrical engineers, and computer scientists of TUD, RWTH Aachen and Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mikro- und Optoelektronik mbH (AMO) in Aachen, Forschungszentrum Jülich (FZJ), Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics Halle (MPI-MSP), Nanoelectronic Materials Laboratory gGmbH (NaMLab) in Dresden, Ruhr-Universität Bochum (RUB).

For the initial funding phase (April 2025 – December 2028), the TRR404 offers several PhD and Postdoc positions with starting dates from April 1, 2025 onwards. All vacancies can be found here: https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/trr-vacancies (https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/trr-vacancies) .

For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.

At TUD the TRR404 offers, subject to the availability of resources, a full-time position as

Research Associate (m/f/x)

(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited to 24 months with the option of extension subject to further projects. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification. Balancing family and career is an important issue. The position is generally suitable for candidates seeking part-time employment. Please indicate your request in your application.

Position#5:              TRR404-TUD-B06

Project:                     B06 System Models, Architectures, and Application Mapping Tools 

Project Leader:    Prof. Jeronimo Castrillon (Chair of Compiler Construction)

Tasks:

The PhD student will be mostly in charge of modeling operations of emerging computing architectures, designing compiler abstractions, and working towards a programming framework for the 3D systems.

Requirements: 

- excellent university degree (Master/ diploma or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering or a relevant area
- sound knowledge in C/C++ software development, experience in compilers (LLVM, MLIR) and automatic code optimization, knowledgeable in computer architecture

- willingness and ability to think beyond the boundaries of your field, to act in an international and diverse environment and to live an open and constructive communication
- strong analytic and problem-solving skills, creativity

We offer:

A varied and challenging research task, embedded in a friendly, inclusive and supportive team of the TRR’s Principal Investigators (i.e., project leaders and supervisors). We maintain an open and cooperative work attitude with maximum personal responsibility, mutual support with a solution-oriented approach, and flexible working hours where possible. As a PhD student you will be integrated in the TRR’s Graduate School as well as becoming a member of the TUD’ Graduate Academy. Both will offer tailored educational programs and individual supervision agreements.

In addition, TUD offers: 

- employment in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement for the public service of the Länder (TV-L)
- an individual assignment of the collective agreement experience level taking into account your previous professional experience
- 30 days annual vacation (based on a 5-day workweek) and annual bonus payment (restrictions apply)
- additional pension scheme (VBL)
- very good accessibility by public transport
- car parking facilities
- state-of-the-art buildings with labs equipped to a high technical standard
- a wide range of offers for health promotion and for the compatibility of family and career
- numerous opportunities for further training, including language courses, IT courses and other courses

TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.

Application:

Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents including a motivation letter, CV, copy of degree certificate, transcript of grades (i.e., the official list of coursework including your grades) and proof of English language skills, by October 30, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file quoting the reference number TRR404-TUD-B06 in the subject header to jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de) or to:

TU Dresden, Chair of Compiler Construction, Prof. Jerónimo Castrillón, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.

jobs.occupation: Research Associate / PhD Candidate in Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience (m/f/x) (Neurowissenschaftler/in)
jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (25,8895 hrs/wk = 65%) starting in March 2027, we are looking for 1

Research Associate / PhD Candidate in Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience (m/f/x)

The newly established research group of Prof. Dr. Timothy Zolnik at the Faculty of Biology and Biotechnology, Ruhr University Bochum, investigates how deep cortical neurons influence cortical and thalamic circuits. Our work combines cellular electrophysiology with optogenetics, pharmacology and circuit approaches to study mechanisms relevant to attention and arousal.

The PhD candidate will investigate cellular and synaptic mechanisms in defined cortical circuits, with a focus on layer 6b and its interactions with other cortical and thalamic neurons. The project centers on whole-cell recordings in acute mouse brain slices, combined with optogenetic circuit mapping and quantitative analysis.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 years
Start: starting in March 2027
Apply by:  2026-10-26

Your tasks:

• Design and perform whole-cell patch-clamp experiments in acute mouse brain slices.

• Measure intrinsic neuronal properties and synaptic responses in identified cell types.

• Combine electrophysiology with optogenetic circuit mapping and pharmacological manipulations.

• Perform or assist with stereotaxic viral injections and prepare tissue for recordings and histology.

• Analyze, visualize and interpret electrophysiological data using quantitative methods.

• Document experiments and present results in lab meetings and at scientific conferences.

• Contribute to scientific manuscripts and the collaborative development of the research group.

Your profile:

• A completed Master’s degree (or equivalent) in neuroscience, biology, physiology, biomedical sciences or a related field (required).

• Hands-on experience with whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in acute ex vivo brain slices (required).

• Experience analyzing and interpreting electrophysiological data (required).

• A strong interest in cellular, synaptic and circuit neuroscience, with careful experimental practice (required).

• Very good written and spoken English and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively (required).

• Experience with stereotaxic viral injections and/or optogenetics (desirable).

• Experience with neuropharmacology, histology, microscopy and/or programming for data analysis (advantageous).

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day

As Manager (f/m/d) 9HL PDT, you will lead a global team of highly skilled turbine frame professionals responsible for the SGT-9000HL frame turbine module. You will provide technical and people leadership across product development, design, validation, fleet improvement, and lifecycle support while ensuring effective interfaces with manufacturing, service, procurement, fleet management, product management, and project organizations. You will translate complex technical and business priorities into clear direction, accountable work packages, and timely decisions that strengthen product reliability, performance, cost competitiveness, and customer value.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Lead, coach, and develop a global team of engineering professionals, ensuring strong performance, capability growth, and successful execution of turbine development activities.
* Define and drive the technical strategy, priorities, and execution roadmap for SGT-9000HL turbine-module development, upgrades, fleet improvements, and issue-resolution initiatives.
* Lead complex turbine frame design reviews and technical decision-making across the full product lifecycle, from concept development through manufacturing, testing, verification, validation, and product release.
* Direct technical programs, root cause analyses (RCA), and design down-selection activities, ensuring delivery within quality, schedule, and budget targets.
* Own resource planning, budget allocation, and manpower management, while establishing robust engineering processes and clear work packages to achieve business objectives.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration across Engineering, Manufacturing, Service, Procurement, and Project organizations to support fleet performance, market introduction, customer communication, and long-term technology roadmap execution.

What You Bring

* Master’s degree or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a comparable engineering discipline
* Extensive experience in gas turbine product design and development, including turbine frames, hot gas path components, and mechanical integrity
* Advanced expertise in gas turbine engineering, heat transfer, turbine module development, and relevant engineering tools such as Siemens NX, Teamcenter, and SAP
* Proven leadership and development of diverse, global engineering teams, including coaching, resource planning, and performance management
* Strong project management and strategic planning capabilities, including experience with Agile or KANBAN methodologies
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, including business-fluent English and German and coordination across Manufacturing, Service, and Procurement

About the Team

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.  

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

As a Senior Principal Peptide Scientist External API Development (m/f/d), you shape the chemical foundation of our peptide pipeline by defining and delivering phase-appropriate drug substance strategies, synthetic routes, manufacturing processes, and supply solutions through an external CDMO network. In this role, you represent Drug Substance Chemistry within the global CMC Technical Development team and are accountable for the drug substance contribution to the overall CMC package. Apply if you want to combine scientific leadership with strategic decision-making and pragmatic execution across development and manufacturing.

- You lead the design, evaluation, and optimization of synthetic routes and manufacturing processes for peptide APIs, balancing speed, quality, safety, cost, sustainability, scalability, and process understanding
- You define phase-appropriate drug substance strategies and select suitable peptide synthesis, purification, isolation, and manufacturing approaches
- You Provide scientific expertise on protecting-group strategies, coupling and deprotection, aggregation, epimerization, oxidation, impurity formation, purification, isolation, and stability

- You represent Drug Substance Chemistry in cross-functional CMC project teams and contribute to CMC strategy, risk assessment, development planning, supply planning, and regulatory documentation

- Lead process transfers across external partners and into internal development or manufacturing organizations, ensuring knowledge continuity, documentation, troubleshooting, and compliance falls under your responsibility

WHO YOU ARE

- You hold a PhD in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, peptide chemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a closely related scientific discipline
- You bring strong expertise in peptide drug substance development and manufacturing, including solid-phase, liquid-phase, hybrid, fragment-based, and emerging synthesis technologies
- Your hands-on experience in API process development, scale-up, manufacturing, and scientific troubleshooting within an external CDMO model sets you apart
- You demonstrate a solid understanding of phase-appropriate CMC requirements, including strategy development, risk assessment, development and supply planning, and CMC documentation

- You communicate clearly and manage stakeholders effectively in global, cross-functional project environments while making pragmatic decisions
- You apply a strong quality, regulatory, safety, sustainability, and data integrity mindset in development and manufacturing activities

Salary: €90,000 – 120,000 / year, depending on experience | Permanent | Immediate start | Bexbach

Why join us?

- Strategic ownership: you own your categories globally, not just execute someone else's sourcing plan
- Direct influence on P&L through savings, cost modeling, and supplier negotiations
- Hands-on role combined with strategic scope — close to sites, not just headquarters theory
- Hybrid working possible where travel and supplier meetings allow [please confirm extent]
- 28 days of vacation, plus Rosenmontag, Christmas Eve, and New Year's Eve automatically off

About us – in brief

Headquartered in Bexbach, KD Pharma Group is a mid-sized, internationally active company and one of the world's few manufacturers of Omega-3 concentrates with a purity of up to 99.5% – built on a sole focus on Omega-3 fatty acid research and technology development.

- Own assigned categories globally: develop sourcing strategies, benchmark markets, and drive competitive positioning
- Lead supplier business reviews and category meetings, ensuring alignment across Procurement, Technical, and Operations
- Identify and qualify new suppliers to enhance competitiveness and reduce supply risk
- Lead complex supplier negotiations leveraging cost breakdowns, volume leverage, and market trends
- Develop and execute negotiation playbooks with the Strategic Sourcing Specialist
- Manage long-term agreements, payment terms, and escalation clauses in line with group governance
- Build and maintain cost models, track raw material indices, and perform variance analysis
- Analyze supplier quotations, freight trends, and payment terms to determine total cost of ownership (TCO)
- Maintain and improve supplier relationships through structured performance reviews and scorecards
- Partner with QA/Technical teams to resolve non-conformances and ensure preventive actions
- Lead cross-functional alignment on material specifications, MOQ rationalization, and cost-saving projects
- Act as mentor and point of escalation for sourcing or supplier-related issues within the Procurement team

Qualifikation

Must-have

jobs.description:
The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The following full-time (38.5 hours/week) position is to be filled as soon as possible at the Center of Neurology of the University Hospital Bonn:

Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease (m/w/d)

The position is fixed-term until 30 September 2028 due to the duration of the research project.

Parkinson’s disease is usually diagnosed only after substantial neurodegeneration has already occurred. Subtle changes in movement, facial expression and speech may emerge years earlier, but current clinical assessments are not designed to detect and quantify them at scale. We believe that computer vision and multimodal AI can help close this gap - and that meaningful progress requires researchers who want to apply cutting-edge methods to a major clinical challenge.

Our goal is to develop objective and scalable digital tools for the early detection and monitoring of Parkinson’s disease. We combine video-based analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and limb movements with speech, touchscreen and wearable sensor data. A particular focus is on individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, who are at high risk of developing Parkinson’s disease or related neurodegenerative disorders.

The group of Prof. Dr. Michael Sommerauer at the Center of Neurology at the University Hospital Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will take a leading role in the development of the computer vision components of bradyMX, our multimodal digital motor assessment platform. The position is embedded in the ERC-funded Re-START PD research program and offers the opportunity to work with unique, deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts and longitudinal datasets. Rather than developing methods in isolation, you will work closely with clinicians and neuroscientists to translate methodological advances into tools that may improve patient stratification, clinical trials and, ultimately, the way Parkinson’s disease is detected.

Please submit your application as a single PDF, including: 

• a cover letter describing your scientific interests and motivation for joining the group 

• a curriculum vitae including a publication list 

• contact details for at least two referees

Your responsibilities:

- Lead the development of computer vision methods for quantifying subtle motor abnormalities from clinical video recordings
- Develop robust pipelines for human pose estimation, facial and body landmark detection, movement segmentation, tracking, feature extraction and automated quality control
- Design and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning models for the analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and upper- and lower-limb movements
- Investigate temporal modelling, representation learning and interpretable movement features for the detection and monitoring of early motor dysfunction
- Integrate video-derived features with complementary digital modalities such as speech, touchscreen tasks, inertial sensors and clinical assessments
- Evaluate model robustness and generalizability across participants, recording conditions, devices and international study sites
- Work closely with the clinical research team on study design, data collection, annotation strategies and the interpretation of model outputs
- Prepare scientific manuscripts, present results at international conferences and contribute to grant applications
- Support the supervision of doctoral, Master’s and medical students

Your profile:

- - A doctoral degree in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, biomedical engineering, medical informatics or a closely related discipline
- Strong experience in machine learning and deep learning for image, video or human movement analysis
- Excellent programming skills in Python and practical experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX
- Experience in one or more of the following areas: human pose estimation, motion tracking, action recognition, temporal modelling, self-supervised learning, multimodal learning or domain adaptation
- A sound understanding of experimental design, quantitative model evaluation and reproducible research practices
- Experience with version control and collaborative software development; knowledge of containerized workflows and high-performance computing is an advantage
- Interest in translating methodological advances into clinically meaningful applications; previous experience in Parkinson’s disease or medical research is welcome but not required
- A high degree of scientific curiosity, independence and commitment to rigorous research
- Strong communication skills and enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international environment
- Very good command of written and spoken English; German language skills are not required

What we offer: 

- The opportunity to lead an innovative research project at the intersection of computer vision, multimodal AI, neurology and digital health
- Access to unique, deeply phenotyped cohorts of individuals at risk of Parkinson’s disease, healthy controls and patients with early Parkinson’s disease
- Rich video, sensor and clinical datasets collected using standardized multimodal assessment protocols
- A direct path from methodological development to external validation and clinically relevant application
- Close collaboration with neurologists, neuroscientists, and international experts in Parkinson’s disease and digital biomarkers
- An excellent research environment at the University Hospital Bonn, the University of Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases
- Access to modern computational infrastructure and support for reproducible data analysis and software development
- Strong support for scientific publications, conference participation, grant applications and the development of an independent academic profile
- Opportunities to supervise junior researchers and contribute to a growing interdisciplinary research group

Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.

Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA Biology

The Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.

As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience. This work is supported by extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure.

Tackling critical questions on PTB functions in A. thaliana using a multidisciplinary approach, which integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, and plant stress physiology
Applying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biology
Developing an integrated framework to decipher PTB’s role in splicing and its downstream physiological outcomes, with a particular focus on drought stress
Assisting with lab organisation and other general tasks
Contributing to teaching activities for Bachelor's and Master's students within our group
Supervising PhD students and other group members
Presenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscripts

Experience with a spectrum of molecular methods

Teaching experience is a plus, but not mandatory
Very good English language skills (at least level B2); German language skills are a plus, but not mandatory

A fascination for science, very good communication and teamwork skills
